checks_run.procedure: Probe A, the reviewer's own AUD sweep generated from the contract. First populate every P3 record type by running the seven P3 exercise seams. Then call each of the 64 P3 mutating operations as the org-wide read-only auditor, with every path parameter filled from an existing row and If-Match "1". Send two bodies: {} and a plausible body with transformationId and initiativeId. Expect 403 with exactly one audit event, authorization.denied. Finally, checksum every row of all 29 P3 tables before and after the sweep.
checks_run.command: bash with-pg.sh 26310 pnpm vitest run --project integration apps/api/test/integration/zz-sec-r1/sec-r1-aud-sweep.test.ts (copied from probes/; Node 22, LANG unset), and again with probe B (26312, Node 24, LANG=C.UTF-8)
checks_run.environment: Disposable clone $TMPDIR/review-p1 at ec45ef1; PostgreSQL 16 (SQL_ASCII and UTF8 clusters)
checks_run.expected: 403 + ['authorization.denied'] on every call; no P3 table changes.
checks_run.actual: 66/66 tests pass on Node 22 (LANG unset) and on Node 24 (LANG=C.UTF-8). 128 calls were made. Every call with a target got 403 and exactly one authorization.denied event, and all 29 table checksums are identical before and after. Two kinds of call have no target to authorize against. (a) The empty body on the seven top-level creates whose scope is in the body: createInitiative, createT08Dependency, createCapacity, createResourceDemand and createFundingDecision answer 400 validation, and createBusinessCase/createBenefitFormula answer 403 through the holdsAnywhere gate. All of them write nothing. (b) checkBenefitFormula is a write-free check with no transformation; it answers 403 with nothing written. The probe was revised twice before this run, and both earlier runs failed only on the probe's own bodies. Revision 1 failed 8 tests because the empty body on top-level creates gave 400. Revision 2 failed 3 tests because createResourceDemand and createFundingDecision take initiativeId, not transformationId, and because checkBenefitFormula correctly records no denial when there is no target. Each revision is documented in the probe header.

checks_run.procedure: Static and suite review of authorization on every P3 write path: openWrite with atCommit (refreshPrincipal inside the write transaction), validation, If-Match, and an audit event. Also check for client or remote I/O inside a transaction, and confirm that every P3 GET has a read gate.
checks_run.command: diff-scan.log S1 (openWrite/atCommit per module), S7 (remote I/O), GET-handler scan; integration logs grep 'commit time|BE18A'
checks_run.expected: Every P3 mutation re-authorizes at commit time, and no non-database await runs inside a transaction.
checks_run.actual: Every openWrite call in the P3 write modules (portfolio/*, kpi business-case/line/formula/version/calculation, workflows T08) passes { atCommit: true }. dependency-types.ts calls refreshPrincipal(tx) directly. runInitiativeAction runs the read gate (404), then the write gate at commit (403), then validation, then If-Match + FOR UPDATE + version check (428/409), then the step and its audit. No fetch, fs or request-stream use exists in these modules (S7 none). Every P3 GET resolves its record and calls requireTransformationRead, directly or through readCase, readFormula or readVersion. The only exceptions are the authenticated catalogues of dependency types and formula examples. 25 commit-time/BE18A integration tests pass in each run. Observation, not raised: the product-gate submit and decide routes reused for G4 are DG2-approved P2 operations, not among the 109. They still authorize on the request's principal, which is resolved in preValidation after the body has arrived, and do not use refreshPrincipal. The residual window is the handler's own execution. These routes are unchanged in kind from DG2.

checks_run.procedure: Probe C, a hostile-input and correctness probe of packages/shared/src/formula. C1: 41 injection strings (JS code, prototype names, unicode digits, comments, NaN/Infinity). C2: hostile sizes, including in-limit depth and node cases. C3: division by zero anywhere in the tree. C4: 20,000 random strings over the token alphabet plus raw UTF-16. C5: 3,000 random + - * / trees checked against an independent BigInt-rational oracle with half-up rounding to 6 dp. C6: hostile inputs keys.
checks_run.command: pnpm vitest run --project unit-node packages/shared/src/formula/zz-sec-r1-fuzz.test.ts (copied from probes/), on Node 22 and Node 24
checks_run.expected: Never throws; nothing outside the grammar evaluates; limits refuse as formula.syntax quickly; division by zero gives null (Unknown); stored result = oracle; inputs cannot inject values.
checks_run.actual: 65/65 pass on both Node versions. Grammar-invalid strings return ok=false, null. '-0' evaluates to 0, and that is a valid expression. Limits: too_long for >2000 characters (1e5 parens, 1e6 chars, 10k terms); too_deep for 900 nested parens and 40 nested abs(); too_many_nodes for a 150-term sum; number_digits for a 25-digit literal; all in <1 ms. A product of 100 x 24-digit values gives result_out_of_range in 23 ms, and 99 chained divisions return inexactIntermediate=true in 7 ms. Division by zero gives null with formula.division_by_zero in all 7 shapes. 20,000 fuzz strings: no throw, slowest 8.6 ms, 83 valid ones evaluated to plain decimals. Oracle: 2,853 trees match exactly, including 1,577 that needed rounding, and every tree that is exact at 6 dp has rounded=false. __proto__/constructor keys cannot satisfy a variable. Code review: evaluate.ts uses decimal.js at precision 80 with an exactness oracle, Map lookups for variables, Object.create(null) for the inputs record and own-property checks. The rounding record is on the row (0027 CHECKs bind rounded/stored to the columns, NOT VALID rounding_required for new rows), and benefit_calculation is append-only (p2_attach_append_only) (diff-scan.log S8).

checks_run.procedure: Check that the formula engine has no dynamic code path and that the ESLint override (backed by the fuzz.test.ts source scan) enforces this against bypass forms. Part 1: a new file under formula/ containing the five named forms and six bypass candidates, run through eslint. Part 2: the bypasses appended to evaluate.ts, then eslint plus the engine's source-scan test.
checks_run.command: npx eslint packages/shared/src/formula/zz-lint-probe.ts; npx eslint packages/shared/src/formula/evaluate.ts; pnpm vitest run --project unit-node packages/shared/src/formula/fuzz.test.ts -t 'source scan' (disposable clone; files removed or restored afterwards)
checks_run.expected: There is no dynamic code in the engine, and the guard refuses every way of building code from a string.
checks_run.actual: The engine has no dynamic code: the S6 scan is empty. Part 1, eslint exit 1 as designed: the five named forms (eval, new Function, setTimeout(string), .constructor(...), import()) are refused, and the six bypasses produce no error: Reflect.construct(Function, …), globalThis['ev'+'al'], createRequire(import.meta.url)('vm'), Reflect.apply(Function, …), computed ['constructor'], and alias F = Function. Part 2: with five bypasses inside evaluate.ts, eslint exits 0 and the source scan passes. In Node the alias form returns 42 for 'return 6*7'. The guard therefore does not enforce the ADR-0024 §6 'no dynamic code' rule against these forms. Raised as F-DG3-100 (Low, non-mandatory): the coverage gap is real and the shipped engine is not affected.
